10.1002_aenm.202505223: The practical implementation of lithium metal batteries (LMBs) requires overcoming the challenges posed by unstable interphase between Li metal and electrolyte, particularly under high areal capacities. Continuous chemical corrosion and non‐uniform plating/stripping degrade the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), causing rapid capacity loss and safety risks. Herein, we propose a molecular bridged (MB) hybrid interphase integrated with dual silane coupling agents, enabling highly reversible Li anodes at high areal capacities in carbonate‐based electrolyte. The MB layer tightly anchors Li metal by chemical bonding, prevents delamination during high‐capacity Li deposition/dissolution, and decouples parasitic reaction from Li deposition by an anti‐corrosive coupling network. Consequently, the MB‐stabilized Li anode achieves an impressive cycling for 600 h at 1 mA cm −2 , and 8 mAh cm −2 , and sustains 474 cycles at 1 C with 80% capacity retention in Li||LiFePO 4 full cell. Furthermore, an Ah‐level pouch cell with high cathode loading (NCM811, ≈ 45.9 mg cm −2 ) maintains stable cycling at low N/P ratios (≈1.87). This strategy for constructing a molecular‐bridged interphase offers a new perspective for maintaining the artificial SEI integrity under harsh conditions, demonstrating the feasibility of durable, high‐performance LMBs with reduced Li loss.
10.1002_aenm.71784: Surface texturing in crystalline silicon solar cells imposes a fundamental trade‐off in perovskite‐silicon tandems: micrometer‐scale pyramids enable efficient light trapping but limit the conformal deposition of thin perovskite films with sub‐micrometer thickness, whereas reduced texture heights improve compatibility at the expense of optical performance and interfacial quality of the tandem device. Here, we address this challenge by combining precisely controlled submicron texturing with an ozone‐assisted chemical rounding treatment. The resulting silicon substrates feature smoothly rounded, symmetric submicron textures that suppress micro‐terrace formation and partial epitaxy at the amorphous silicon/crystalline silicon interface, while promoting more spatially uniform optoelectronic properties in the subsequently integrated top‐cell stack. The morphology‐engineered texture yields a monolithic perovskite–silicon tandem device with a power conversion efficiency of 33.25%, demonstrating that multiscale morphological control provides a powerful pathway to simultaneously improve the optical performance and interfacial quality of tandem solar cells.
10.1002_anie.202505751: Potassium–sulfur (K–S) batteries are emerging as one of the most promising candidates for next‐generation energy storage, owing to their high energy density and cost‐effectiveness. However, the severe polysulfide shuttle effect and sluggish redox kinetics of sulfur cathodes remain critical barriers to their practical application. Herein, a class of organosulfur‐rich porous carbon (OSPC) has been developed as a high‐performance cathode for soluble‐polysulfide‐free and high‐rate K–S batteries. The as‐constructed OSPC achieves molecular‐scale confinement of sulfur species within the carbon skeleton via covalent bonding, which enables solid–solid sulfur redox pathways without generation of electrolyte‐soluble polysulfides. Moreover, the conductive carbon skeleton of OSPC with well‐developed porosity can facilitate potassium ion and electron transport within the bulk cathode and significantly improve sulfur redox kinetics. Benefiting from these integrated merits, excellent high rate capability (240.8 mAh g −1 at 5 A g −1 based on the mass of OSPC), long‐term cycling stability (77% retention after 500 cycles at 5 A g −1 ), and remarkable areal capacity (4.5 mAh cm −2 ) can be achieved for the OSPC cathodes. Additionally, the feasibility of synthesizing OSPC from real‐world waste plastics is demonstrated, which offers a dual benefit of alleviating plastic pollution and enabling the fabrication of low‐cost yet high‐performance cathodes for K–S batteries.
10.1002_anie.5938299: Understanding and controlling atomic‐level interactions within multicomponent alloys provides a promising avenue to drive multistep tandem catalysis. Herein, we develop an atomic symmetry‐breaking PtFeCoCu multicomponent alloy that disrupts long‐range order and local coordination homogeneity and identify the nature of its enhanced performance for oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The deliberate symmetry breaking, featured by heterogeneous local coordination and anisotropic strain, enriches the Pt environment with additional transition‐metal neighbors. These distortions activate multicomponent interactions and tune the Pt electronic structure, promoting ORR intermediate conversion while suppressing component dissolution. Consequently, PtFeCoCu reaches a half‐wave potential of 0.95 V RHE and a mass activity of 3.53 A mg Pt −1 at 0.9 V RHE in ORR. In an H 2 ‐O 2 fuel cell, it delivers a high mass activity of 1.63 A mg Pt −1 at 0.9 V iR‐free , retaining 87.7% of its initial mass activity after 30,000 cycles. Our findings highlight symmetry breaking as a key driver with broad implications across multicomponent alloys.
10.1021_acssuschemeng.6c07437: Photo-Fenton reactions have attracted significant interest for water decontamination, but their practical application is limited by iron (Fe) aggregation and narrow pH windows. Precursor chemistry plays a critical yet underexplored role in regulating the spatial distribution and catalytic accessibility of iron in carbon-based photo-Fenton catalysts. Manipulation of Fe sites distribution to tune catalytic accessibility of Fe on carbon dots (CDs) constitutes a topic of vast interest and a challenging pursuit. Here, we report a precursor-directed strategy to develop Fe atomically surface-accessible CDs (Fe-SACDs), with excellent response to simulated solar light, using shrimp-extracted chitin as a precursor. A controlled spatial distribution of atomically dispersed Fe centers was enabled by the abundant nitrogen- and oxygen-containing functional groups in the chitin precursor. The surface-accessible Fe species enabled robust Fe(II)/Fe(III) cycling, which enhances the generation of reactive species for catalysis of organics in water. These advantages afforded highly efficient degradation of methylene blue (∼100% removal) with improved structural stability (more than 5 cycles) and broader pH adaptability (3–12) compared to nonsurface-accessible controls where Fe is absent (CDs) or not atomically dispersed (Fe-CDs). This study reveals how a precursor-directed control of Fe spatial distribution governs the performance of photo-Fenton catalysis, inspiring a new strategy for designing efficient biomass-derived carbon catalysts for advanced water decontamination.
10.1021_jacs.6c08995: Although the optimized structures of the photoactive species have driven a rapid development in third-generation solar cells in the past decade, minimizing interfacial loss is another critical factor for achieving high-performance devices. Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) have emerged as an effective approach to modulate the interface between materials to enhance device performance and stability, serving as alternatives to the conventional polymeric hole-transporting layers. In this Review, we first provide a systematic analysis on each structural component of SAMs, while elucidating the underlying mechanisms of their characteristic advantages. Furthermore, we investigate their applications in both perovskite solar cells and organic photovoltaics, emphasizing their role in highly efficient solar cells. Finally, we propose the future research direction of the field for large-scale manufacturing and commercialization. The structure-property relationships discussed in this Review will serve as a foundation for the optimized designs of SAMs, offering insights into achieving theoretical limits in next-generation devices.
10.1029_2026ef008707: Urban pluvial flooding is often summarized by peak depth, peak extent, or cumulative burden, but these metrics do not distinguish when flooding first becomes hazardous from when the hazardous area becomes largest. This study introduces an activation–occupancy framework to quantify these two times and applies it to building‐resolving shallow‐water simulations of Manhattan ( at m resolution) under an Ida‐derived hyetograph and New York City's 1‐hr design storm. Under the Ida‐derived rainfall at the 0.3‐m threshold, district activation peaks occur within a 35‐min span, whereas the times of maximum hazard extent are much more dispersed. Under the shorter design storm, peak timing compresses sharply. Rainfall is spatially uniform in both simulations, so the 35‐min activation spread reflects routing alone and provides a lower bound on the variability of activation timing; spatial rainfall heterogeneity lies outside the modeled scenarios. Across the two modeled rainfall scenarios, severe‐flooding geography remains broadly consistent: the same seven districts exceed the borough reference at 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4 m, with the strongest rank preservation for eventual extent and hazardous area–time burden. At 0.5 m, that set contracts to six because Lower East Side/Chinatown falls just below the borough reference in both scenarios. East Harlem remains the principal exception in design‐storm timing at the deeper thresholds. These diagnostics distinguish severity patterns relevant to adaptation from scenario‐specific timing information for warning and response.
10.1039_d5ta09558a: Hierarchically porous Sb 2 O 3 –Bi 2 O 3 nano-leaves on nickel foam enable efficient energy storage and water splitting. Synergistic effects and oxygen vacancies deliver 1738 F g −1 capacitance and low overpotentials of 112 mV (HER) and 248 mV (OER).
